issues.legal_issue: A plaint amendment adding a new declaration may be refused when it would defeat a limitation right that accrued to the opposing party before the amendment was sought.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a pending partition suit and later sought to add a declaration challenging a registered deed affecting the property.
The opposing parties had pleaded the deed in their written statement, and the amendment application was made about three years after that pleading.
Allowing the amendment would have permitted a claim for declaratory relief after the time for bringing that claim had expired.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was properly refused because it would defeat the opposing parties’ accrued right to rely on limitation; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, amendments are ordinarily allowed, but an amendment is refused in exceptional cases where it takes away a legal right accrued through lapse of time. The Court relied on Laxmidas Dahyabhai Kabarwala v. Nunabhai Chunilal Kabarwala, distinguishing a merely clarificatory amendment from one that adds a new claim or relief. Registration of the deed gave notice to persons claiming an interest in the property, and the written statement in any event disclosed the deed to the plaintiff.

rule.if: amendment_in_pending_civil_suit and amendment_adds_new_claim_or_relief and limitation_right_accrued and amendment_would_defeat_accrued_right

predicates.amendment_in_pending_civil_suit: A party sought to amend pleadings in a pending civil suit.
predicates.amendment_adds_new_claim_or_relief: The proposed amendment added a claim or relief rather than merely clarifying an existing pleading.
predicates.limitation_right_accrued: The opposing party had acquired a limitation-based right because the time to bring the added claim had expired.
predicates.amendment_would_defeat_accrued_right: Allowing the amendment would take away the opposing party’s accrued limitation-based right.

issues.definition: When an amendment in a pending civil suit adds a claim or relief, a limitation-based right has accrued, and allowing the amendment would defeat that right, the amendment is refused.
